items.question: What is in a .NET assembly compared to a JavaScript module?
items.answer: An assembly packages IL, metadata describing all types and members, and a manifest with name and version. One DLL can contain hundreds of types. JavaScript modules are typically source files or bundles resolved by import paths with package.json versioning. .NET loads assemblies through the CLR with binding and compatibility rules — FileNotFoundException on mismatch, not ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
followUps: What does InternalsVisibleTo solve for unit tests?
How does NuGet relate to assembly references?
items.sixtySeconds: Assembly is IL plus metadata plus version. Not one class per file. NuGet ships assemblies.

items.question: Explain AssemblyLoadContext and when you use a collectible ALC.
items.answer: Default ALC loads shared runtime and app assemblies — not unloadable. Custom collectible ALC loads plugin DLLs in isolation; Unload() reclaims plugin metadata when no references remain. Use for hot-reload plugins or script engines. Loading plugins into Default ALC means you cannot unload without restarting the process.
followUps: How does LoadFromAssemblyPath differ from default loading?
items.sixtySeconds: Default ALC for app. Collectible ALC for plugins. Unload when refs gone. Not Default for hot swap.

items.question: When is reflection the wrong tool?
items.answer: Per-message dispatch by string method name on a hot SQS path — slow, not refactor-safe, breaks trimming. Reflection is fine once at startup for DI registration or scanning handlers. Prefer source generators or switch on typed discriminators for hot paths. Native AOT requires DynamicallyAccessedMembers roots if you must reflect.
followUps: How do source generators replace reflection for JSON?
items.sixtySeconds: Reflection at startup OK. Per request bad. Generators and switches for hot paths.

items.question: What is DynamicallyAccessedMembers and why does Native AOT care?
items.answer: Trimming and Native AOT remove metadata for types not proven reachable. DynamicallyAccessedMembers annotates reflection entry points so the analyzer preserves required members. Without roots, publish succeeds but runtime throws MissingMethodException. Prefer source-generated serializers over annotated reflection on hot paths.
followUps: How does JsonSerializerContext avoid the problem?
items.sixtySeconds: Trim removes unreferenced metadata. DynamicallyAccessedMembers roots types. Generators better than roots on hot path.

items.question: How do you prevent breaking changes in a shared NuGet library?
items.answer: Treat public types as contract. Use internal for experiments. CI runs PublicApiAnalyzers or ApiCompat against a baseline — fails on removed or changed public members without approval. Semantic versioning: breaking change bumps major and updates baseline. Pair with nullable and analyzer warnings as errors in library projects.
followUps: Is adding a new public method breaking?
What about changing record positional parameter order?
items.sixtySeconds: Public API is contract. CI diff. internal by default. Major bump for breaks.

items.question: What attributes does the C# compiler honor directly?
items.answer: Obsolete produces warnings or errors. Conditional removes call sites unless symbol defined. Nullable context attributes flow into metadata for flow analysis. Most framework attributes like Required or HttpGet are read by libraries at run time, not special-cased by the compiler itself — except where they affect nullable analysis.
followUps: Difference between attribute on property vs field for validation?
How do source generators read attributes?
items.sixtySeconds: Compiler: Obsolete, Conditional, nullable. Framework attributes read at runtime or by generators.

items.question: How do source generators differ from reflection for JSON on an SQS consumer?
items.answer: Reflection serializer inspects properties per message — CPU and allocation cost, trim-unsafe. JsonSerializerContext generator emits typed serialization at compile time — no per-message reflection, Native AOT friendly. Measure CPU with dotnet-trace before and after on representative message volume.
items.sixtySeconds: Generator emits code at build. Zero per-message reflection. JsonSerializerContext for SQS hot path.

items.question: Your plugin host leaks memory after unloading plugins — what do you check?
items.answer: Collectible ALC only unloads when no Assembly, Type, or delegate references remain from Default ALC. Static events, cached delegates, or ThreadStatic holding plugin types pin the ALC. Use weak references or isolate plugin interfaces loaded only in the collectible context. dotnet-gcdump shows rooted plugin types after Unload().
followUps: What does InternalsVisibleTo affect in plugin loading?
items.sixtySeconds: Collectible ALC needs zero refs from outside. Static caches pin plugins. gcdump for roots.
